content: Lipin-1 is a protein in humans that is encoded by the LPIN1 gene. Lipin-1 exhibits phosphatidate phosphatase activity, which is crucial for lipid metabolism. Its localization within the nucleus is regulated by the mammalian Target of Rapamycin (mTOR) protein kinase. This regulation connects mTORC1 activity to the control of gene transcription that is dependent on Sterol Regulatory Element-Binding Proteins (SREBPs). The LPIN1 gene is considered a candidate gene for human lipodystrophy, a condition characterized by the loss of body fat, fatty liver, elevated triglyceride levels (hypertriglyceridemia), and insulin resistance. Studies in mice indicate that this gene plays a role in normal adipose tissue development and may also contribute to triglyceride metabolism in humans.
